attorneys.name: Barbara (Barbi) H. Agricola
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Opelika, AL
attorneys.bio:
Barbi Agricola, founder of Agricola Law, concentrates her practice in the areas of plaintiff's personal injury law, family law and criminal defense. Barbi was born and raised in Montgomery, where she attended LAMP High School, a nationally-ranked college preparatory school. She completed her undergraduate work at the University of Alabama in Birmingham, where she was accepted into the school's prestigious University Honors Program, which only accepts fifty students a year. Barbi graduated magna cum laude with University and Departmental honors, earning a major in Political Science and a double minor in Criminal Justice and Philosophy and Law, all within the span of three years.

After College at UAB, Barbi attended law school at the University of Alabama School of Law in Tuscaloosa, where she received numerous awards for her trial advocacy skills, leadership skills and involvement in the law school. She was a member of the Order of the Barristers, the Bench & Bar legal honor society, and Law School Ambassadors, among others. Barbi also served as the Managing Editor of the Law & Psychology Review, where she also had a legal article published. As part of the school's trial advocacy and moot court teams, she won first place at the National Trial Advocacy Competition in one year and in another year advanced to the quarter-final rounds in moot court competition.

After law school, Barbi completed several federal clerkships, including clerking for the Honorable William M. Acker, Jr. of the Northern District of Alabama, the Honorable Joel F. Dubina, then Chief Judge of the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals, and the Honorable W. Keith Watkins, Chief Judge of the Middle District of Alabama. These experiences enable Barbara to maintain a vibrant federal court practice with a high level of knowledge and skill.

attorneys.name: Algert S. Agricola Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Election Law Lawyers in Opelika, AL
attorneys.bio:
Algert S. Agricola, Jr. was admitted to the Alabama Bar in 1978. Al received his Bachelor of Arts from Tulane University of Louisiana in 1974 and his Juris Doctorate from the University of Alabama School of Law in 1978. He served as Law Clerk and Staff Attorney, for the Alabama Court of Criminal Appeals from 1978 to 1980. He served as Law Clerk to Judge Truman M. Hobbs, U.S. District Court, Middle District of Alabama, in 1980. Al was appointed Assistant Attorney General for the State of Alabama, Civil Litigation Section, and served from 1980 to 1987. Al served in the administration of President Ronald Reagan as an Assistant U.S. Attorney, Middle District of Alabama, Criminal Division and Civil Forfeitures from 1987 to 1989. Al’s experience as a federal prosecutor gives him unique insight into the system as a defense attorney. Al is a member of the Montgomery County Bar Association and the Alabama State Bar Association. His practice concentrations are in election law, constitutional law, long term care, insurance coverage analysis, mental health law, employment practices litigation, premises liability, administrative law, and white-collar crime. Al has been appointed to serve as a Special Assistant Attorney General while in private practice to represent the interests of the State of Alabama and its employees. He is currently serving as an Administrative Law Judge for the State of Alabama. Al is a past president of the Hugh Maddox Inn of Court and is current president of the Montgomery Chapter of the Federalist Society.

Over his almost four decades as a lawyer, Al has represented seven Alabama governors, three chief justices of the Alabama Supreme Court, four associate justices of the Alabama Supreme Court, and numerous circuit and district judges. Recently, Al was appointed by the Alabama Supreme Court to serve on its Standing Committee on the Alabama Rules of Appellate Procedure.

attorneys.name: Mary Katherine Alemany
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Auburn, AL
attorneys.bio:
Mary Katherine is a native of Huntsville, Alabama. She is a graduate of Auburn University with a Bachelor of Arts in Sociology. During her time at Auburn, she was involved in the Auburn Pre-Law Scholars Program. Upon graduating from Auburn in August of 2014, Mary Katherine attended Cumberland School of Law at Samford University in Birmingham, Alabama. While in law school, Mary Katherine served as class Treasurer, a member of the Student Bar Association, the law school representative for the Samford University Graduate Student Council, an instructor for the Street Law Program, and was selected as a member of the Harvey S. Jackson Excellence in Teaching Award Committee. After passing the Alabama Bar Exam in July of 2017, Mary Katherine began practicing in Randolph County, Alabama. She joined Akridge & Balch in June of 2023 and her primary focus is criminal defense, family law (divorce, custody, adoptions, termination of parental rights, child support), and juvenile delinquency and dependency. Mary Katherine has zealously represented hundreds of criminal clients, ranging from simple traffic citations to attempted murders, and everything in between. She serves Lee County, Randolph County, and all surrounding areas.

Mary Katherine is a certified Guardian Ad Litem and a member of Alabama Criminal Defense Lawyers Association, National Criminal Defense Lawyers Association, Lee County Bar Association, Randolph County Bar Association and the Alabama State Bar Association. Mary Katherine and her husband, Matt, reside in Opelika, Alabama with their two sons, Wally and John Henry, and their two dogs, Waylon and Ophelia. During her free time, Mary Katherine enjoys all things live music, reading, and chasing after her wild boys. She and her family are active members of Church of the Highlands.

He joined the firm in 1999, after receiving his law degree from the University of Alabama School of Law, graduating magna cum laude. During Law School, Mr. Alves was a member of the Alabama Law Review, the Bench and Bar Legal Honor Society, and the John A. Campbell Moot Court. He was honored as a Hugo Black Scholar and is currently a member of the Order of the Coif.

His practice emphasizes business, construction and real estate litigation in State and Federal Courts, while also practicing in the areas of municipal law, probate, wills, estates and real property.

Mr. Alves is a member of the Baldwin County Bar Association and the Alabama Bar Association. He is a member of the board of directors for several non-profit corporations including the Boys and Girls Club of South Alabama, the Daphne/Spanish Fort Rotary, the American Red Cross, and the Alabama Free Clinic, which provides free medical services to the working uninsured in Baldwin County.

attorneys.name: Charles L. Anderson
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Montgomery, AL
attorneys.bio: Charles L. Anderson is the founder and managing partner of Anderson, Williams, & Farrow, LLC, with offices in Montgomery, Alabama, and Jackson, Mississippi. A native of Montgomery and a graduate of Sidney Lanier High School, he was a recipient of the Jimmy Hitchcock Memorial Award as a high school Senior in 1978. Anderson earned his BA degree from Furman University in Greenville, South Carolina, where he is a member of Omicron Delta Kappa honorary society and the Furman University Athletic Hall of Fame. He received his J.D. from Samford University’s Cumberland School of Law in 1985 where he attended on an NCAA Post-Graduate Scholarship. Upon graduation, Anderson served as a law clerk to the Honorable H. Randall Thomas, Presiding Judge of the 15th Judicial Circuit in Alabama. He was admitted to practice law in the state and federal courts in Alabama in 1985. His practice encompasses a broad range of civil litigation and mediation. He has been the principal provider attorney for LegalShield in the state of Alabama since 1991. He is a member of the American Bar Association, the Alabama State Bar, and the Montgomery County Bar Association where he has served on the Board of Directors. He has been on numerous committees for the Alabama State Bar. He is a past president of the Montgomery County Young Lawyers and has served as Chairman of the Alabama State Bar Committee on Pre-Paid Legal Services, and the Alabama Young Lawyers Section Executive Committee. Anderson is a member of the Alabama Association for Justice Board of Governors, the American Association for Justice, and is a Master of the Bench and Past President of the Hugh Maddox Chapter - American Inns of Court. He possesses the AV peer review rating by Martindale-Hubbell. A registered mediator with the Alabama Center for Dispute Resolution, Anderson has completed course work in mediation offered by the American Arbitration Association and The Program of Instruction for Lawyers at the Harvard Law School. He regularly provides pro bono service as a mediator in the Montgomery County Small Claims Court.

attorneys.name: William D. Anderson
attorneys.practice_type: Condominium Law Lawyers in Mobile, AL
attorneys.bio:
Born in Nurnberg, Germany at U.S. Army Hospital on March 29, 1978, Will grew up in Enterprise Alabama where he received his primary education. Will graduated from Enterprise High School in 1996 and went on to attend Birmingham-Southern College.

While attending BSC, Will spent time in Washington, D.C. as an intern to Senator Richard C. Shelby, and as a member of Kappa Alpha Order, he had the privilege of donating his services to The Muscular Dystrophy Association, American Cancer Society, Habitat for Humanity and many other worthy organizations.

After graduating from Birmingham-Southern with a degree in Accounting, Will attended Campbell University where he obtained his law degree and Masters in Business Administration in 2003. While in law school, Will served as an associate editor for The Campbell Law Observer and was a member of Phi Alpha Delta legal fraternity.

Will joined the firm in 2003 after graduation, and is a member of the Firm's Alabama and Florida practices where he focuses on the areas of insurance law, condominium law, construction law and personal injury law. Will has also been admitted to practice in all Federal Courts in Alabama, as well as the Northern District of Florida. Will became a partner in the Firm effective January 1, 2009.

Will is a member of the American Bar Association, Alabama Bar Association, Florida Bar Association, Baldwin County Bar Association, Escambia-Santa Rosa Bar Association, Community Association Institute, and Rotary International.

Will is a frequent contributor and author of articles for Condo Owner magazine. He also regularly participates as a presenter and speaker at the Condo Owner Educational Symposium held annually in the coastal communities of Gulf Shores and Orange Beach, Alabama.

Will, Sarah, daughter Caroline, and their son William reside in Fairhope where they attend the Fairhope United Methodist Church. In his spare time, Will enjoys fishing and is an avid fan of The Alabama Crimson Tide and Atlanta Braves.

attorneys.name: W. R. Rip Andrews
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation & Appeals Lawyers in Birmingham, AL
attorneys.bio:
Rip Andrews always thinks of himself as an underdog, which gives him the drive and diligence to represent clients in a prepared and professional way. He does what it takes to level the playing field and hold opponents accountable.

"I want to make a tangible impact on people's lives. At Marsh, Rickard & Bryan, we do our best to right the wrongs done to those at no fault of their own," says Andrews.

Andrews says that when you put the information gathered during the preparation of the case along with a deep understanding of the clients' expectations, the lawyer's job is to craft a story the jurors will understand.

"When I'm in the courtroom, I want to feel as if I'm talking WITH the jury, not TO them."

attorneys.name: Angela Stewart Ary
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Huntsville, AL
attorneys.bio:
Angela S. Ary is a native of Columbus, Ohio. Ms. Ary became a "southern transplant" in May, 2003.

Practice Areas:

Bankruptcy

Business/Commercial Litigation

Business Transactions

General Corporate Law

Intellectual Property - (Trademark & Copyright)

Ms. Ary represents a number of small to mid-size businesses involved in all aspects of a business's life cycle. Ms. Ary has experience in handling business formations, contract drafting, applications for federal trademark registration, stock issuances, corporate recordkeeping, collections, and dissolutions.

Ms. Ary has gained a great deal of knowledge and experience in representing consumers and businesses in Chapters 7, 13 and 11 bankruptcy cases. Ms. Ary has represented many small business owners in the winding up of company affairs and the individual's Chapter 7 or Chapter 13 bankruptcy case.

Mr. Ary's recent representations have included:

Serving as co-local counsel to the Liquidating Trustee for the Estates of Verilink Corporation and Larscom Incorporated.

Serving as lead Chapter 11 bankruptcy counsel for Johnson Systems, Inc.

Serving as Chapter 11 bankruptcy counsel for the jointly administered cases of Blue Ridge Newspapers, Inc., Cape Fear Newspapers, Inc., Montgomery County Newspapers, Inc. and West 10 Newspapers, Inc.

Serving as association counsel for over 19 homeowners associations in Madison, Limestone and Lauderdale Counties.

Ms. Ary was born in Columbus, Ohio and graduated from Reynoldsburg High School in 1995. She attended The Ohio State University as an Academy student in 1994-1995. Ms. Ary graduated magna cum laude from the University of Tennessee, Knoxville in 1999 with a Bachelor of Arts degree from the College Scholars honors program. In 2002, Ms. Ary graduated from the University of Cincinnati, College of Law with a J.D.

attorneys.name: Lisa Bailey
attorneys.practice_type: Boating Accidents Lawyers in Birmingham, AL
attorneys.bio:
Lisa was born and bred in Columbia, South Carolina, where she earned her undergraduate degree from the University of South Carolina. Throughout her time in South Carolina, she interned for U.S. Congressman James E. Clyburn; the experience she gained in those four years fueled her desire for a career in which she could advocate for those who need it most.

After college, Lisa moved to Birmingham where she earned both her JD and MBA degrees at Samford University. She went to law school with the express purpose of fighting for the underrepresented.

During her time in law school, Lisa served as Chief Justice of the Honor Court and competed on the National Negotiation Team. From there, Lisa clerked for a Civil Circuit Court Judge in Jefferson County and, when that term was over, she immediately began working as a Plaintiff's attorney.

Lisa has successfully settled hundreds of pre-litigation and pre-trial cases and has tried multiple District Court cases to verdict. Lisa enjoys taking an active role in every aspect of the cases she handles and is not afraid to go to court to fight for her clients. She truly understands the devastating impact that a wreck of any size can have on the life of an individual.

attorneys.name: Stephanie Renee Bain
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Pell City, AL
attorneys.bio:
Pell City Alabama family law attorney

Understanding that client comfort and satisfaction are the keys to client retention, Stephanie Bain, P.C. prides itself on always providing a friendly and comfortable work environment. Located in Pell City, our law firm gives clients personalized treatment and honest evaluations. By focusing our practice within several distinct practice areas, we often assist clients multiple times, building trusting and long-lasting relationships.

Born and raised in Pell City and St. Clair County, Stephanie Bain has continued to be an active member of the community. Formerly a 6th grade teacher at a local elementary school, Stephanie Bain now takes time to speak at schools regarding government and serves as past president and board member of the Day Program Board which focuses on counseling, treatment and education programs for children in need. She is also a past officer of the Chamber of Commerce and on the board of the Association for Retarded Citizens. With strong connections to the community and its people, this family law attorney recognizes the value of being a strong and compassionate advocate for clients.

Our Pell City divorce law firm also provides client representation in the areas of criminal law, personal injury, probate and residential real estate. Further, we assist clients in a variety of other family law disputes including custody, paternity, child support, visitation, and juvenile matters. Within criminal law, we take on all cases except capital murder and rape. Finally, our personal injury practice handles industrial workplace injuries, automobile accidents, wrongful death suits and slip and fall accidents.

attorneys.bio:
Caleb W. Ballew joined the firm of Martinson & Beason, P.C. as an associate attorney in October 2012. Caleb’s practice areas include divorce, domestic relations, criminal defense, general civil litigation and estate litigation. In addition, he is a certified guardian ad litem and often represents the rights of juveniles.

Caleb was admitted to practice law in Alabama in 2010 and is a member of the Huntsville-Madison County Bar Association, the Family Law Section of the Alabama State Bar, and the Alabama Criminal Defense Lawyers Association.

attorneys.name: James C. Barton Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Alternative Dispute Resolution Lawyers in Birmingham, AL
attorneys.bio:
Jim is a partner in the Litigation Practice Group and the Chair of the Products Liability Practice Team of Johnston Barton. Jim specializes in products liability cases, with an emphasis on the defense of manufacturers and distributors of pharmaceuticals and medical devices.

Jim has been retained as primary, coordinating, and local defense counsel in hundreds of single-plaintiff and multi-plaintiff cases involving such products. With over 29 years of litigation experience in this practice area, his understanding of the unique interests and concerns of industry clients allows him to work creatively with corporate and national counsel to achieve the best possible outcome in every case.

Jim has defended matters on behalf of manufacturers and distributors in the pharmaceutical industry involving the following products:

•NSAID

•Cephalosporin Antibiotic

•Tricyclic Glycopeptide Antibiotic

•SSRI

•DES

•Fen-Phen

•Insulin

•Antimetabolite

•Narcotic

•Methylphenidate Hydrocloride

•PPA

•Hormone Replacement Therapy

•Anti-Psychotic

•COX-2 Inhibitor

•OTC Products

•Gadolinium Based Contrast Agents

•Acne Skin Care Products

•Dopamine Agonist

•Promethazine Hydrochloride

•Phosphodiesterase Inhibitors

•Pergolide Mesylate

•Metoclopramide

•Products in Clinical Trials.

He has also defended matters on behalf of manufacturers and distributors in the medical device industry involving the following products:

•Pedicle Screws

•Latex Gloves

•Heart Balloon Catheters

•Blood Sugar Monitors

•Extremity MRI Machines

•Insulin Pumps

•Bone Cements

•Narcotic Patches

•Electrosurgical Devices

•Trocars

•Vena Cava Filters

•Morcellators

•Numerous Internal and External Orthopedic Prosthetic and Fixation Devices.

Jim has extensive experience in defending matters on behalf of manufacturers and distributors of equipment used in the construction, trucking, farming, mining and timber industries including the following:

•Dozers

•Front-End Loaders

•Coal/Earth Movers

•Drag Lines

•Cranes

•Skidders

•Skid-Steer Loaders

•Multi-Piece Rims

•Scaffolding

•Diesel Engines.

Jim's product liability experience includes the defense of manufacturers and distributors of products in a number of other industries including:

•Toxic Chemicals

•Tires

•Foods

•Gas and Electric Appliances

•Roofing Materials

•Motor Vehicles

•Specialized Military Equipment

•Firearms

•Propane Tanks

•Computer Software.

Jim has trial and mediation experience, and has practiced in numerous State and Federal Courts throughout Alabama and the Southeastern United States. He is admitted to practice in Alabama, and all appropriate Federal Courts. He is a member of the American Bar Association, the Alabama State Bar and the Birmingham Bar Association. He has served in various capacities in all three bar associations. Jim has received a rating from Martindale-Hubbell that indicates he has reached the height of professional excellence and has been recognized for the highest levels of skill and integrity. He is listed in Best Lawyers in America and Super Lawyers.

Jim currently serves as Co-Chair of the Medical Device Subcommittee of the Products Liability Committee of the ABA Section of Litigation, and as a member of the Pharmaceutical Subcommittee and Mass Torts Committee. He is also a member of the Product Liability Advisory Council, the International Association of Defense Counsel, the Defense Research Institute, the Alabama Defense Lawyers Association and a Fellow of the Litigation Counsel of America.

Jim is also active in the community, currently serving in his twenty-third year as a member of the Altamont School Board of Trustees, where he has served as President, Vice President, Chair of the Headmaster Search Committee, and Chair of the Ten-Million-Dollar Campus Development Committee.

Jim previously served as a member of the Board of Trustees and Vice President of the Legal Aid Society of Birmingham, as Chairman of the Finance Committee of the Alabama State Bar Association, a member of the faculty of the Alabama Bar Institute for Continuing Legal Education, and a member of the faculty of the Cumberland Institute for Continuing Legal Education.

Jim received his degree from the University of Alabama School of Law (J.D., 1981), where he served as Managing Editor of the Law and Psychology Review and was a member of the Bench and Bar Legal Honor Society. He earned his undergraduate degree from Amherst College (B.A., cum laude, 1975).

Jim is an avid outdoorsman and currently serves on the Board of Directors of the Cahaba River Society. He formerly served as a member of the Board of Directors of the Birmingham Canoe Club. He and his wife, Anne, daughter, Jessie Kate, and son, Jim III, enjoy traveling together, particularly to France, as Anne teaches French and Jessie Kate was a French major in college.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Jim is a partner in the Litigation Practice Group and the Chair of the Products Liability Practice Team of Johnston Barton. Jim specializes in products liability cases, with an emphasis on the defense of manufacturers and distributors of pharmaceuticals and medical devices.

Jim has been retained as primary, coordinating, and local defense counsel in hundreds of single-plaintiff and multi-plaintiff cases involving such products. With over 29 years of litigation experience in this practice area, his understanding of the unique interests and concerns of industry clients allows him to work creatively with corporate and national counsel to achieve the best possible outcome in every case.

Jim has defended matters on behalf of manufacturers and distributors in the pharmaceutical industry involving the following products:

•NSAID

•Cephalosporin Antibiotic

•Tricyclic Glycopeptide Antibiotic

•SSRI

•DES

•Fen-Phen

•Insulin

•Antimetabolite

•Narcotic

•Methylphenidate Hydrocloride

•PPA

•Hormone Replacement Therapy

•Anti-Psychotic

•COX-2 Inhibitor

•OTC Products

•Gadolinium Based Contrast Agents

•Acne Skin Care Products

•Dopamine Agonist

•Promethazine Hydrochloride

•Phosphodiesterase Inhibitors

•Pergolide Mesylate

•Metoclopramide

•Products in Clinical Trials.

He has also defended matters on behalf of manufacturers and distributors in the medical device industry involving the following products:

•Pedicle Screws

•Latex Gloves

•Heart Balloon Catheters

•Blood Sugar Monitors

•Extremity MRI Machines

•Insulin Pumps

•Bone Cements

•Narcotic Patches

•Electrosurgical Devices

•Trocars

•Vena Cava Filters

•Morcellators

•Numerous Internal and External Orthopedic Prosthetic and Fixation Devices.

Jim has extensive experience in defending matters on behalf of manufacturers and distributors of equipment used in the construction, trucking, farming, mining and timber industries including the following:

•Dozers

•Front-End Loaders

•Coal/Earth Movers

•Drag Lines

•Cranes

•Skidders

•Skid-Steer Loaders

•Multi-Piece Rims

•Scaffolding

•Diesel Engines.

Jim's product liability experience includes the defense of manufacturers and distributors of products in a number of other industries including:

•Toxic Chemicals

•Tires

•Foods

•Gas and Electric Appliances

•Roofing Materials

•Motor Vehicles

•Specialized Military Equipment

•Firearms

•Propane Tanks

•Computer Software.

Jim has trial and mediation experience, and has practiced in numerous State and Federal Courts throughout Alabama and the Southeastern United States. He is admitted to practice in Alabama, and all appropriate Federal Courts. He is a member of the American Bar Association, the Alabama State Bar and the Birmingham Bar Association. He has served in various capacities in all three bar associations. Jim has received a rating from Martindale-Hubbell that indicates he has reached the height of professional excellence and has been recognized for the highest levels of skill and integrity. He is listed in Best Lawyers in America and Super Lawyers.

Jim currently serves as Co-Chair of the Medical Device Subcommittee of the Products Liability Committee of the ABA Section of Litigation, and as a member of the Pharmaceutical Subcommittee and Mass Torts Committee. He is also a member of the Product Liability Advisory Council, the International Association of Defense Counsel, the Defense Research Institute, the Alabama Defense Lawyers Association and a Fellow of the Litigation Counsel of America.

Jim is also active in the community, currently serving in his twenty-third year as a member of the Altamont School Board of Trustees, where he has served as President, Vice President, Chair of the Headmaster Search Committee, and Chair of the Ten-Million-Dollar Campus Development Committee.

Jim previously served as a member of the Board of Trustees and Vice President of the Legal Aid Society of Birmingham, as Chairman of the Finance Committee of the Alabama State Bar Association, a member of the faculty of the Alabama Bar Institute for Continuing Legal Education, and a member of the faculty of the Cumberland Institute for Continuing Legal Education.

Jim received his degree from the University of Alabama School of Law (J.D., 1981), where he served as Managing Editor of the Law and Psychology Review and was a member of the Bench and Bar Legal Honor Society. He earned his undergraduate degree from Amherst College (B.A., cum laude, 1975).

Jim is an avid outdoorsman and currently serves on the Board of Directors of the Cahaba River Society. He formerly served as a member of the Board of Directors of the Birmingham Canoe Club. He and his wife, Anne, daughter, Jessie Kate, and son, Jim III, enjoy traveling together, particularly to France, as Anne teaches French and Jessie Kate was a French major in college.

attorneys.name: Christopher S. Berdy
attorneys.practice_type: Drug and Device Litigation Lawyers in Birmingham, AL
attorneys.bio:
When asked to describe what the phrase "nonstop advocate" means to him, Chris Berdy says it's an unwavering dedication to service before self. It means placing the interests of clients, the firm and the community above his own interests.

Chris first learned this dedication to client service while working at his father's periodontal practice. As a boy, Chris's father immigrated with his family to Ellis Island from post-WWII Europe. He had nothing and spoke no English at the time. Dr. Berdy ultimately earned his education and established a successful service-based business where Chris worked throughout his childhood.

Chris says his father and other mentors have taught him that he can overcome any challenge through perseverance and a positive attitude. He takes this approach when counseling Christian & Small's product manufacturing, health care and business clients with their legal matters

attorneys.name: Shelley L. Bilbrey
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Huntsville, AL
attorneys.bio:
Shelley comes to Northern Alabama from middle Tennessee where she spent most of her childhood and adolescence. After receiving a Bachelor's of Psychology from Belmont University, Shelley began working as a social worker for six years at a non-profit organization, Davidson County Juvenile Court and lastly the Tennessee Commission on Children and Youth. During that time, Shelley also received a Master's in Counseling from Trevecca Nazarene University. In 2000, Shelley began a new aspect of her career when she began attending the University of Alabama School of Law. Shelley graduated in 2003 and began a clerkship with Madison County Circuit Judge Loyd H. Little that fall. Spring 2004 was the beginning of Shelley's private law practice when she became an associate attorney at Grace, Evans & Matthews working in insurance defense law. Shelley was fortunate enough to soon have the opportunity to move into domestic relations law at the beginning of 2005. From January 2005 to February 2008, Shelley worked at William P. Burgess, Jr., P.C. where she learned the practice of domestic relations law from her mentors Bill Burgess, Esquire and Judge George Craig. Shelley opened her practice in February 2008, offering clients a variety of ways to resolve domestic cases, including uncontested actions, contested litigation, and collaborative resolutions.

Shelley has a variety of interests outside of the practice of law, such as reading, playing guitar and singing, photography, and building furniture with very basic woodworking skills. She loves the mountains and appreciates the arts and crafts of glass, wood, and metals.

attorneys.name: Brett M. Bloomston
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Birmingham, AL
attorneys.bio:
BRETT M. BLOOMSTON is a partner in The Bloomston Firm in Birmingham, Alabama. He concentrates his practice in the areas of criminal defense, white collar crime, DUI and general litigation.

Mr. Bloomston has served as an adjunct professor at the Miles College, School of Law where he taught Evidence and Criminal Law. He has lectured on evidence, criminal trial practice, DUI defense and serving as appointed counsel at various continuing education seminars throughout the State. Mr. Bloomston has been featured as a commentator on Court TV's, "In Session."

Mr. Bloomston served as the President of the Greater Birmingham Criminal Defense Lawyers Association, is a Life Member of the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, is a member of the Alabama Criminal Defense Lawyers Association, the Birmingham Bar Association's Criminal Procedure Committee, and the Birmingham Inn of Courts.

Mr. Bloomston is recognized as one of Alabama's Super Lawyers and is rated by Martindale-Hubble as AV, that group's highest rating and Birmingham's Top Attorneys in criminal law. Mr. Bloomston is a 1993 honors B.A. graduate from the University of Alabama and earned his J.D. in 1996 from the University's School of Law.

attorneys.name: Ralph Bohanan Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Products Liability Lawyers in Birmingham, AL
attorneys.bio:
Ralph was born in Oxford, England the son of United States military parents. He graduated from West Point High School.

Ralph graduated from Cumberland School of Law in Birmingham, Alabama in 1987. While in law school, Ralph participated in many mock trial competitions. Ralph was the winner of the Samford University Cumberland School of Law James O'Haley trial competition. Ralph's trial team then won the southeast regional mock trial championships sponsored by the American Association for Justice. Thereafter, Ralph's team won the prestigious national mock trial championship held in Washington, D.C. sponsored by the American Association for Justice.

Upon graduating from law school, Ralph began his law career as a defense attorney exclusively representing physicians, nurses and hospitals in medical malpractice lawsuits. After two years, Ralph elected to change direction and began practicing in a large Birmingham, Alabama personal injury firm wherein he became a partner. Four years ago, Ralph chose to open his own law firm. Since 1989, Ralph has been involved in claims alleging: faulty products, automobile crashworthiness, vehicle rollovers, medical malpractice, insurance fraud and bad faith, automobile accidents, trucking accidents, workers compensation claims, alcohol related accidents, third party work related injuries and personal injuries of a large scope.

Ralph has spoke at many seminars wherein the topics have been Automobile and Truck and Semi-Truck Accidents, Workers Compensation and On the Job Injuries, Medical Malpractice and Legal Discovery Issues.

Ralph is admitted to practice in all state and federal courts in Alabama and the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit.

attorneys.name: Mike Bowling
attorneys.practice_type: Breach of Warranty Lawyers in Birmingham, AL
attorneys.bio:
Mike Bowling has practiced law in Birmingham Alabama since obtaining his J.D. from the University of Alabama School of Law in 1996. He began his practice with a large defense firm before leaving with several of his partners to start his own firm in 1998. Mr. Bowling's practice over the last 20 years has consisted primarily of work on the defense side, which gives him a unique perspective on how to best counter the arguments often made by defense counsel. His plaintiff practice began to grow over the last several years, which led to his recent decision to join Morgan & Morgan and represent plaintiffs, both businesses and individuals, full time. He has litigated cases for both the plaintiff and defense in 10 states and tried cases to verdict in five. Before leaving his firm to join Morgan & Morgan earlier this year he obtained several verdicts/settlements on behalf of plaintiffs.

These verdicts/settlements include a $5.75 million jury verdict in Georgia Federal Court against an engineering firm whose defective design work caused damage to an explosive facility located in Tennessee, a $7.3 million settlement in a breach of fiduciary duty case on behalf of two individuals whose business was stolen from them by unscrupulous business partners, a $2.5 million settlement on behalf of a family whose mother was killed in an accident involving an 18 wheeler, a $1 million dollar settlement against a medical device manufacturer in favor of a hospital and surgical practice, and a $500,000 settlement in favor of a family whose son was killed in an accidental shooting. While Mr. Bowling truly enjoys trying cases to verdict, his real love of the practice of law has always centered around the bond formed with clients as a result of helping them through some of the most difficult times of their lives. This is what led him to join Morgan & Morgan and dedicate himself to plaintiff practice for the remainder of his legal carrier.

Mr. Bowling has an AV rating through Martindale-Hubbell, the highest available to any lawyer. Over the years he has also served on the Council for Litigation Management, been a member of the Alabama Society of Explosives Engineers, served on the board of the local YMCA, and assisted with the trial team for the Cumberland School of Law located in Birmingham, Alabama.

attorneys.name: Sara G. Bragdon
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Auburn, AL
attorneys.bio:
Primarily practicing in the areas of estate planning, elder law, special needs planning, and probate matters, Sara is able to provide peace of mind to her clients, often during difficult times in their lives, and relieve a lot of the stress that can often be associated with aging and ill loved ones. Sara's passion is helping clients through all stages of their estate planning, from young families ensuring that they have a guardian named for their minor children to elderly clients as they transition to the next phase in their care. As a result, Sara believes in treating her clients like family and believes that the ability to plan your estate and having documents prepared by a professional is not a luxury reserved for the wealthy, but a necessity for everyone.

Sara and her husband, Ben, live in Auburn with their two boys and their four-legged canine daughter, Colby. Sara is an avid LEGO builder and fierce "mat mom," cheering on her oldest son at jiu jitsu tournaments year round. As Auburn residents, the Bragdons live for football season and gymnastics season.

attorneys.name: D. Ty Brown
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Birmingham, AL
attorneys.bio:
Ty Brown grew up in a family of lawyers and sees his entry into the legal profession as a natural course to maturity. At an early age, he was taught to do the right and honorable thing in all his relationships.

"I learned that the law applies to everybody," Brown says.

Most clients who come to Marsh, Rickard & Bryan, P.C., are in desperate situations, which happened through no fault of their own. They are at the end of their rope and need understanding and hope. "I remember one case in particular where a young man had been very seriously injured. I understood then and there that my worst day will never be as bad as his best," Brown says. "There are people who need us to get through some of the most trying times of their lives."

Like his father and brothers before him, Ty likes being in the courtroom. "I like to look the witnesses and jury in the eye and see into their hearts. I am telling the client's story and I must tell it well. I have learned to do this at Marsh, Rickard & Bryan."

attorneys.name: Jason Daniel Bruner
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Opelika, AL
attorneys.bio:
Jason built his legal career on a foundation of service, discipline, and realworld leadership. He joined the United States Army in 2010 and spent the early years of his career as an Engineer Officer during the Global War on Terror. In 2013, he deployed to Afghanistan as a Platoon Leader, supporting combat operations and leading soldiers in demanding, highpressure environments. Those experiences shaped his approach to problemsolving: stay calm, stay prepared, and take care of the people who rely on you.

In 2018, he transitioned into the Judge Advocate General’s Corps and served as a Judge Advocate until 2024 when he left active duty and joined the U.S. Army Reserve. His work spanned administrative law, military justice, and criminal prosecution. He served as Senior Trial Counsel for the 3rd Infantry Division and was twice selected as a Brigade Judge Advocate—once in South Korea at Camp Casey with the 210 Field Artillery Brigade, and again stateside at Fort Benning, GA—advising commanders, training leaders, and ensuring legal readiness across large organizations. His reputation for clear judgment, steady leadership, and meticulous preparation followed him throughout every assignment.

After completing activeduty service, he continued his commitment to public service as an Assistant Attorney General in the Special Prosecutions Division, where he handled public corruption cases for the State of Alabama. He also continues to serve in the U.S. Army Reserve as a Judge Advocate.

Jason's academic path reflects the same drive for excellence. He graduated from Florida State University in 2010, then earned his law degree from Cumberland School of Law, graduating cum laude, in 2018. While at Cumberland, he served as an Associate Editor of the Cumberland Law Review, sharpening the writing and analytical skills that now support his litigation work.

attorneys.name: Raymond C. Bryan
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Anniston, AL
attorneys.bio:
Ray Bryan grew up on a dairy farm in Ashland, Alabama and attended Clay County High School. Upon graduation he entered the U.S. Army Security Agency as the war in Viet Nam was coming to an end where he obtained a Top Secret Crypto Security Clearance in his work as an electronic warfare specialist. After completion of his military service Ray returned home to Alabama and began his college education at a community college in Alexander City, Alabama. It was there on the front steps of the church in 1978 that his Pastor at Calvary Heights Baptist Church in Alexander City introduced Ray to his beautiful wife, Robin. They have now been married almost 38 years. They have two daughters and four wonderful grandchildren.

Ray obtained his undergraduate degree from Jacksonville State University. He then earned his juris doctorate degree from Cumberland School of Law at Samford University in Birmingham, Alabama. Ray has been practicing law in Anniston for over 27 years. He maintains a general practice of law and has experience in business law, family law, civil law, criminal law and probate and estate law. He is a member of the Alabama Bar Association and the Calhoun County Bar Association.

Ray appears each Friday on Trinity Broadcasting Radio (WTBJ) that is broadcast across east Alabama and west Georgia with Dr. Grinstead on the Front Porch Fellowship where he answers legal questions from a Christian perspective. He has served and been in leadership positions on the boards of various local charities and civic organizations. He is a Director of Harvest Time International in Sanford, Florida that ministers to the poor around the world. Ray and his wife presently attend Church of the Highlands in Gadsden, Alabama.

David was born in Mobile, Alabama on July 5, 1973, and grew up in Fairhope, Alabama, where he received his primary education. David graduated from Fairhope High School in 1992.

David attended Troy University on an academic scholarship. While attending Troy, he was a member of the Gamma Beta Honor Society, Environmental Club and the Sigma Alpha Epsilon National Fraternity. In 1996, David graduated Cum Laude from Troy with a BS in Environmental Science.

After graduating from Troy, David attended Mississippi College School of Law on an academic scholarship. He graduated Cum Laude and obtained his J.D. degree in 1999.

David is a member of the Mississippi Bar (admitted 1999), Alabama Bar (admitted 2004), Georgia Bar (admitted 2005) and Texas Bar (admitted 2005). David, his wife, Joanna, and their daughters, Nicole and Reagan, reside in Fairhope where they attend the Fairhope United Methodist Church. In his spare time, David enjoys hunting, fishing, exercising and sports.

Trey came to work for Morgan and Morgan in December 2021 because he wanted to help victims of personal injury cases get the representation and justice they deserve.

attorneys.name: Lewis Carter
attorneys.firm_name: Gardberg & Kemmerly, P.C. Attorneys at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Veterans' Disability Lawyers in Mobile, AL
attorneys.bio:
Born in Toms River, New Jersey, Lewis and his family moved to Stapleton, Alabama, when he was three years old. After graduating from high school, he attended the University of West Florida, graduating in 2010. Unsure what direction to go in, but wanting to make a difference, he first decided on a career on education. It wasn't long before Lewis realized that the best way to bring about the change he wanted would be to pursue a career in law. Enrolling in Savannah Law School, Lewis launched his legal career by interning with Legal Services Alabama, where he assisted with SSI and SSDI claims, and later PetersonDelleCave, where he helped victims of police misconduct in New York. After graduating from Savannah Law School, he was admitted to the practice of law in Alabama in 2018.

Prior to starting work at Gardberg and Kemmerly in 2021, Lewis opened a small solo practice in 2018, focusing on bankruptcies before expanding into criminal defense. During this time, he also worked with the South Alabama Volunteer Lawyers Program, handling bankruptcies for low-income clients. In September of 2020, he took a contract with the City of Mobile as an indigent defense attorney, working there until February 2021. Toward the end of 2020, Lewis expanded his practice again, once more working with Legal Services of Alabama, where he assisted tenants facing eviction as the result of the Covid pandemic.

attorneys.name: Andy Citrin
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Mobile, AL
attorneys.bio:
Professional Background and Legal Philosophy

Before Andy started his own business, he worked with a prestigious trial firm as an appellate lawyer. He quickly gained a reputation as one of Alabama’s leading experts on appeals, punitive damages, products liability law, procedure, evidence, tort reform, and protecting trial records. During his appellate years, Andy argued scores of appeals to the Alabama Supreme Court, many involving cases of first impression and many more involving seven- and eight-figure verdicts. Remarkably, Andy handled 17 appeals simultaneously with over $100 million worth of verdicts and five cases of first impression challenging the tort reform package passed by the Alabama legislature in 1987.

The Alabama Supreme Court appointed Andy to serve on the Alabama Pattern Jury Instruction Committee. Andy also served as editor for the Alabama Trial Lawyers Journal and served on numerous local rules committees. He has published papers and given lectures to large groups of lawyers and judges across Alabama.

Andy was featured on the Alabama Super Lawyers 2009 list and in the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum. He is board-certified as a civil trial advocate. Andy is one of the top 100 trial lawyers in Alabama and is recognized by the Bar Register as one of the community’s most eminent professionals. Andy has been AV rated (the highest peer rating available) for more than 17 years. In addition to these distinctions, the firm has been named on the Bar Register of Preeminent Law Firms by Martindale-Hubbell for the past 10 years. In 2017, his law firm was named one of Alabama’s best companies to work for.

Another passion of Andy’s is his Safe Driving Program, entitled D.A.N.G.E.R.S. He taught this safe driving course to thousands of local high school students in coastal Alabama and plans to continue this work. His message to the students: “Drive safely and put me out of business!”

Family and Personal Life

Andy grew up on the blue waters of Hollywood, Florida, the fifth of six children. He left Florida to attend Tulane University in New Orleans, Louisiana. At Tulane, he served as president of the Kappa Sigma fraternity. Andy graduated with a Bachelor of Arts degree in economics in 1983. He then attended Cumberland School of Law in Birmingham, Alabama. Andy served as the articles editor for the American Journal of Trial Advocacy and was awarded the Curia Honoris award by the law school faculty and graduated cum laude.

Andy is married to Jeannie Little Citrin, and they have four children: Sarah, Katherine, Andy, and Gigi. They are the joy of his life and his inspiration to continue to fight for justice.

attorneys.name: C. Carter Clay
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Birmingham, AL
attorneys.bio:
Carter was born in Mobile, Alabama on June 23, 1973, and graduated from St. Paul's High School in Mobile in 1991. He attended college at The Citadel in Charleston, South Carolina on an athletic and academic scholarship. During his senior year, he was a member of The Citadel Honor Court. He graduated magna cum laude from The Citadel in the spring of 1995 with a B.S. in Business Administration.

Upon graduating from college, Carter spent the next year working on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C. as a Legislative Correspondent/Assistant to Congressman Tom Latham (Iowa-4th District). In the fall of 1996, Carter entered Cumberland Law School at Samford University. He received his J.D. Degree from Cumberland in the spring of 1999 and was admitted to practice law in the State of Alabama upon passing the bar exam in the summer of 1999.

Since he started practicing law, Carter has exclusively represented individuals in the areas of civil litigation involving truck and automobile accidents, defective products, medical malpractice, pharmaceutical and medical device litigation, industrial/construction accidents, premises liability, fraud, bad faith and worker's compensation. He has a particular interest and vast experience representing individuals who have sustained severe burns and/or scald injuries. In March of 2010, he was appointed by a U.S. District Court Judge in the Southern District of California to the Plaintiff's Steering Committee in In re Hydroxycut, which involved claims by numerous individuals across the country for injuries after use of the dietary supplement known as Hydroxycut.

Carter handles cases throughout the entire country and has participated in numerous jury trials with great success. In 2012, he obtained a $3 million dollar jury verdict from a Madison County, Alabama jury on behalf of an individual injured in a motor vehicle accident. According to the Alabama Jury Verdict Reporter, this was the largest jury verdict in Madison County for 2012. In 2011, he obtained a $3.5 million dollar jury verdict from a Dallas County, Alabama jury on behalf of the estate of a young boy that died while a residential student at an academy. Prior to 2011, Carter obtained a $1.6 million dollar verdict from a Mobile County, Alabama jury in a defective product case and a $1.45 million dollar verdict from a Leon County, Florida jury in a motor vehicle accident case. These verdicts have allowed him to be an eligible member for the Million Dollar Advocates Forum which consists of attorneys who have obtained verdicts in excess of a million dollars.

Carter is admitted to practice before the Alabama Supreme Court as well as the United States District Courts in Alabama. He is a member of the Alabama State Bar Association, Birmingham Bar Association, Alabama Association for Justice and American Association for Justice. In 2012, Carter was nominated and selected by his legal peers for inclusion in the 2012 edition of Alabama Super Lawyers. Also, he recently served as a board member for the Muscular Dystrophy Association’s Summer Camp Program in Alabama.

Additionally, Carter has been a featured speaker at numerous seminars on topics such as "Recent Developments in the Areas of Spoliation, Subrogation, Mental Anguish and Collateral Source Rule" (ABICLE 2002), "The Automobile Accident from the Civil Side" (ABICLE 2005), "Jury Selection Tips" (Lorman 2006), "Handling Subrogation and Hospital Liens" (ATLA 2006), "How to Effectively Use Video Depositions at Trial" (ABICLE 2007), "Tips on Personal Injury, Product Liability and Mass Torts Litigation" (Barristers 2009) and "Settlements on Behalf of Minors and Settlement Agreements" (Barristers 2010).

Carter is married to the former Heather Ranager, a native of Meridian, Mississippi and 1994 college graduate from the University of Alabama. Carter and Heather have two children, Hollis and Coleman. Carter and his family are members of Mountain Brook Community Church and reside in the Crestline Community of Mountain Brook, Alabama.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Carter was born in Mobile, Alabama on June 23, 1973, and graduated from St. Paul's High School in Mobile in 1991. He attended college at The Citadel in Charleston, South Carolina on an athletic and academic scholarship. During his senior year, he was a member of The Citadel Honor Court. He graduated magna cum laude from The Citadel in the spring of 1995 with a B.S. in Business Administration.

Upon graduating from college, Carter spent the next year working on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C. as a Legislative Correspondent/Assistant to Congressman Tom Latham (Iowa-4th District). In the fall of 1996, Carter entered Cumberland Law School at Samford University. He received his J.D. Degree from Cumberland in the spring of 1999 and was admitted to practice law in the State of Alabama upon passing the bar exam in the summer of 1999.

Since he started practicing law, Carter has exclusively represented individuals in the areas of civil litigation involving truck and automobile accidents, defective products, medical malpractice, pharmaceutical and medical device litigation, industrial/construction accidents, premises liability, fraud, bad faith and worker's compensation. He has a particular interest and vast experience representing individuals who have sustained severe burns and/or scald injuries. In March of 2010, he was appointed by a U.S. District Court Judge in the Southern District of California to the Plaintiff's Steering Committee in In re Hydroxycut, which involved claims by numerous individuals across the country for injuries after use of the dietary supplement known as Hydroxycut.

Carter handles cases throughout the entire country and has participated in numerous jury trials with great success. In 2012, he obtained a $3 million dollar jury verdict from a Madison County, Alabama jury on behalf of an individual injured in a motor vehicle accident. According to the Alabama Jury Verdict Reporter, this was the largest jury verdict in Madison County for 2012. In 2011, he obtained a $3.5 million dollar jury verdict from a Dallas County, Alabama jury on behalf of the estate of a young boy that died while a residential student at an academy. Prior to 2011, Carter obtained a $1.6 million dollar verdict from a Mobile County, Alabama jury in a defective product case and a $1.45 million dollar verdict from a Leon County, Florida jury in a motor vehicle accident case. These verdicts have allowed him to be an eligible member for the Million Dollar Advocates Forum which consists of attorneys who have obtained verdicts in excess of a million dollars.

Carter is admitted to practice before the Alabama Supreme Court as well as the United States District Courts in Alabama. He is a member of the Alabama State Bar Association, Birmingham Bar Association, Alabama Association for Justice and American Association for Justice. In 2012, Carter was nominated and selected by his legal peers for inclusion in the 2012 edition of Alabama Super Lawyers. Also, he recently served as a board member for the Muscular Dystrophy Association’s Summer Camp Program in Alabama.

Additionally, Carter has been a featured speaker at numerous seminars on topics such as "Recent Developments in the Areas of Spoliation, Subrogation, Mental Anguish and Collateral Source Rule" (ABICLE 2002), "The Automobile Accident from the Civil Side" (ABICLE 2005), "Jury Selection Tips" (Lorman 2006), "Handling Subrogation and Hospital Liens" (ATLA 2006), "How to Effectively Use Video Depositions at Trial" (ABICLE 2007), "Tips on Personal Injury, Product Liability and Mass Torts Litigation" (Barristers 2009) and "Settlements on Behalf of Minors and Settlement Agreements" (Barristers 2010).

Carter is married to the former Heather Ranager, a native of Meridian, Mississippi and 1994 college graduate from the University of Alabama. Carter and Heather have two children, Hollis and Coleman. Carter and his family are members of Mountain Brook Community Church and reside in the Crestline Community of Mountain Brook, Alabama.

attorneys.name: Jeremy Cline
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Cullman, AL
attorneys.bio:
Jeremy Cline is an attorney at Lowry, Herren & Cline. A Cullman County native, he graduated from Fairview High School. He earned academic and athletic honors as a track and field athlete at Wallace State and Troy University. He obtained his law degree from Mississippi College School of Law.

Jeremy began his legal career in private practice in 2014 and later served as a prosecutor with the Cullman County District Attorney’s Office before rejoining Lowry, Herren & Cline in September 2022. Due to his diverse background and training, Jeremy is skilled to handle a wide variety of matters, including, but not limited to, personal injury, domestic/custody, and criminal.

In June 2025, Jeremy was appointed to serve as the City Prosecutor for the City of Cullman. This is a part-time position in which Jeremy prosecutes cases to enforce the City of Cullman’s misdemeanor offenses, traffic tickets, and municipal ordinances.

He and his wife, Brittany, live in Cullman with their three children, Sophia, Rory, and Piper, and attend Desperation Church. Jeremy enjoys watching his kids participate in sports and after-school activities, family trips out West and to National Parks, and playing golf.

attorneys.name: David P. Condon
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Transactions Lawyers in Birmingham, AL
attorneys.bio:
Twenty-four years ago, I crossed the Alabama state line at the age of 21 for only the second time in my life. The first time I was a sixth-grade student in Marietta, Georgia on a field trip to the Huntsville Space and Rocket Center.

This second time was in 1991 when I enrolled in law school at Samford University's Cumberland School of Law in Birmingham, Alabama. I graduated from Furman University in 1991 with a degree in Economics and while I never intended to be a lawyer, I thought the law school education could always benefit me no matter what course I ultimately chose. I also knew myself well enough to know that if I were going to pursue additional education following college, it would need to be immediately after college.

Being from Marietta, Georgia, Cumberland School of Law seemed like a good choice as it was fairly close to home and was similar in many ways to Furman University where I spent a wonderful four years and developed meaningful and lasting friendships. So, in August 1991, my mother, father and I packed my belongings in a U-Haul truck and headed west on I-20. As we drove, I considered the journey ahead and where it might take me (in law school, not on I-20) and imagined it would only include a brief three-year stay in Birmingham and a return trip on I-20 East in 1994 to begin a career.

I was surprised to find law school interesting and it did not take long to realize that I could enjoy a nice quality of life in Birmingham. Prior to graduation, I was fortunate to receive an offer of employment from a mid-size law firm and I accepted knowing that my plans to return to Georgia may never come about. It was at this law firm that I learned the importance of a doing a job well, on time and paying attention to detail. I also worked with a great group of people and those friendships developed during those first few years of law practice remain some of my closest today. And, I was lucky to find two mentors that I considered my "professional" father and grandfather that took a real interest in me.

Birmingham was becoming my home and it was about to get even better. In 1996, I took Ashley Herring on our first date to Legion Field for an Olympic Soccer game. Despite having no interest in soccer, Ashley was great company at the game and ignored the absolute downpour that started right at kick off and continued all night. We never thought about leaving the game and Ashley never complained - not once. I knew a good thing when I saw it. In 1997, Ashley and I married and it was the best decision I've ever made. She still has not complained even though I can give her plenty to complain about.

In 2002, I was ready for a change from the world of litigation. Through a chance meeting with my law school classmate Shelly Moss while Christmas shopping for our children (Caroline, at the time 19 months and Paul, 5 months), I learned that Shelly was moving to Texas and leaving her busy real estate closing practice. The prospect of continuing her practice was attractive to me for several reasons. First and foremost however, I liked that I would be providing a needed service at a known and reasonable price for those who chose to be involved in the transaction - not usually the case in litigation.

As I write these words, I feel fortunate to be celebrating my thirteen-year anniversary in the real estate closing business and I have enjoyed it even more than I thought I would. There are many things I like about it including those that I thought I would. But what I find most rewarding, I believe, is that I am a part of a community and I get to play a small part in someone's decision to choose a home.

I enjoy our life here and am proud to call Birmingham home. I'm also grateful that I'm not fighting that Atlanta traffic! Ashley and I have three happy and healthy children (Brian, our third, joined us in 2003) that actually get along and enjoy school.

And, I continue in a job that I find enjoyable and rewarding and always feel flattered when someone allows me to handle their real estate transaction for them. So much so that I hope to be updating this statement another twenty-three years from now!

attorneys.name: Andrew Cooper
attorneys.firm_name: Cooper & Cooper, Attorneys at Law, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Auburn, AL
attorneys.bio:
Andrew Cooper is an attorney at the firm Cooper & Cooper, Attorneys at Law, LLC, situated in Auburn and Phenix City, Alabama. He focuses his practice on criminal defense, child custody, and expungements. He is happy to serve the citizens of Auburn and Opelika because he was born and raised in Lee County. A former Auburn High School student, he attended Auburn University and graduated with a degree in criminal justice. He was later inducted into Auburn University's Criminal Justice Honor Society.

Mr. Cooper was a police officer in the Atlanta area at the time of the bombing at Centennial Olympic Park. Prior to enrolling at Montgomery's Thomas Goode Jones School of Law (affiliated with Faulkner University). He is confident that his knowledge of the law has been enriched by his experiences as a Corrections Officer and Police Officer. He has deep roots in the communities of Lee, Chambers, Russell, Macon, Bullock, Randolph, Tallapoosa, and Montgomery counties, and this, together with his extensive legal training, enables him to provide exceptional representation to these areas.

Because he thinks that everyone is innocent until proven guilty, Mr. Cooper is extremely invested in the field of Criminal Law. He strives for his clients to have both the justice they deserve and the second chances they deserve.

attorneys.name: Benjamin H. Cooper Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Birmingham, AL
attorneys.bio:
Benjamin H. Cooper brings over 20 years of experience working with private and public Fortune 500 companies to his practice of the law. He held executive retail and management positions within the companies, focusing on Corporate Human Resources and Labor and Employment issues, including policy development, training and oversight related to hiring, employment reductions, employment agreements, WARN ACT, organizational reductions in force, and diversity management.

He earned his undergraduate degree from Florida State University and Juris Doctor from the Birmingham School of Law. Benjamin H. Cooper is admitted to practice in the State of Alabama, the U.S. Northern District Court of Alabama and the U.S. Middle District Court of Alabama, and the U.S. District Appeals Court, Eleventh Circuit. He has served as a state-wide mentor working to prepare students for the Alabama Bar Examination, and on the Faculty at the Birmingham School of Law as a Professor of Senior Legal Writing.

Benjamin H. Cooper is a member of The Alabama State Bar, Birmingham Bar Association, The Alabama State Bar Volunteer Lawyers Program, Birmingham Bar Volunteer Lawyers Program, The American Bar Association Labor and Employment Advisory Committee and Equality Alabama, Workplace Chairman, State of Alabama, Jefferson County Mentoring Committee, and other organizations within the Birmingham, Alabama area and surrounding communities.

Benjamin H. Cooper founded the Cooper Law Group LLC and his firm focuses on Labor and Employment litigation, representing the Plaintiff in related issues including the Fair Labor Standards Act, Employment Agreements, Severance Agreements, Non-Compete Agreements, Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, Wrongful Termination, Discrimination, Workplace Harassment, Retaliation, Family Medical Leave Act (FMLA), Collective Bargaining Agreements (Labor Unions) and State Department appeals and hearing processes to include Unemployment Compensation.

Wanting to bring the wealth of knowledge and insight his education and experience has afforded him to a new legal arena, Mr. Cooper has recently announced his candidacy for the position of Executive Director of the ACLU, State of Alabama.

Benjamin H. Cooper was listed among the “Faces of Labor and Employment Law”, and his firm has been featured in numerous publications among the “Top Attorney’s” within the Birmingham, Alabama metro and surround areas.

attorneys.name: Larry G. Cooper Jr.
attorneys.firm_name: Cooper & Cooper, Attorneys at Law, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Auburn, AL
attorneys.bio:
Larry G. Cooper Jr. is an attorney at the firm Cooper & Cooper, Attorneys at Law, LLC, located in Auburn and Phenix City, Alabama. He represents clients with matters including criminal defense, family and civil law, and personal injury. He was born and raised in Auburn, which is located in Lee County, Alabama. In 1987, he got a Bachelor of Arts in Pre-Law Criminal Justice from Auburn University. He was a member of the 1983 SEC champion and 1984 Sugar Bowl victorious Auburn University football team from 1981 to 1984.

While working full-time as an officer for nearly three years, Mr. Cooper pursued law school at Thomas Goode Jones. He graduated in August 1993 and has been practicing law in the Auburn area since April 1994. He joined Sigma Delta while studying law at Jones School of Law. He was voted vice president of the law fraternity in his second year of law school, and then president of the SDK law fraternity in his third year.

And in his last year of law school, Mr. Cooper was elected Chief Justice of the Schools Honor Court, where he presided over student disciplinary hearings and other matters of school-related importance. One year after he graduated from law school, the state of Alabama hired him to work as a law clerk for former Circuit Judge John Davis in Montgomery County Family/Circuit Court, where he did writing and research for Judge Davis and was a special master chosen in pendente lite divorce proceedings.

Mr. Cooper first worked as a solo general practitioner, concentrating on criminal and family law. Cooper & Cooper, Attorneys at Law, LLC was the name given to Larry's legal firm after his brother Andrew Cooper joined him in practice in 2007. Though he serves clients in every county in Alabama, his main areas of concentration are in the state's centralized and eastern regions.

attorneys.name: Samuel N. Crosby
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Daphne, AL
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Crosby practices in the firm's Daphne, Foley and Bay Minette offices. His practice emphasizes the areas of civil litigation, probate practice, trusts, wills, business law, guardianships, estates, real property, estate planning, mediation and death and accident cases. He represents both plaintiffs and defendants.

In 1973, Mr. Crosby graduated with academic distinction from the University of Virginia where he was an All Atlantic Coast Conference soccer player. He received his law degree from the University of Alabama School of Law where he was a member of the Bench and Bar Legal Honor Society and Moot Court Board. He currently serves as a trustee of the University of Alabama Law School Foundation and serves on the Law School Executive Committee.

Mr. Crosby served as president of the Alabama State Bar from 2007-2008. In 2008, he became the first Alabama lawyer to receive the Chief Justice's Outstanding Leadership Award for his service to the public. Since 2009, Mr. Crosby has been included each year in the Alabama Super Lawyers magazine in the practice area of Estate Planning and Probate.

In 2012, Mr. Crosby received the Albritton Pro Bono Leadership Award from the Alabama State Bar. The award recognizes an individual for leadership in making free legal services available to the low income citizens. In 2013, he received the Howell T. Heflin award given by the Mobile and Baldwin County Bar Associations to recognize an Alabama judge or attorney who has brought honor and integrity to the legal profession during his or her years of service to the citizens. In 2016, Mr. Crosby received the Sam W. Pipes Distinguished Alumnus Award from the University of Alabama School of Law. The award is given to an outstanding alumnus who has distinguished himself or herself through service to the Bar, the University of Alabama, and the School of Law. Mr. Crosby received the J. Anthony “Tony” McLain Award from the Alabama State Bar in 2017. The award recognizes outstanding, long-term and distinguished service in the advancement of professionalism by a living member of the Alabama State Bar.

Mr. Crosby has served as president of the Baldwin County Bar Association and is a Life Fellow of the Alabama Law Foundation. This fellowship is based upon dedication to the legal profession and community and is limited to 1% of the state bar association. He is also recognized as a premier mediator, well known for his legal, analytical and conciliation skills. He is one of twenty Alabama mediators selected as a charter member of the Alabama chapter of the National Association of Distinguished Neutrals.

Mr. Crosby has authored two books and numerous professional articles and columns. His book of humorous court stories, The Sleeping Juror (www.sleepingjuror.com), was published in 2002 by the Alabama Law Foundation and has raised over $50,000.00 for Kids' Chance Scholarships and indigent legal services. He has also served on the editorial boards of the Alabama Lawyer and Addendum magazines.

Mr. Crosby served as a local municipal judge and is retired from the JAG Corps of the United States Naval Reserve. He has served as an adjunct professor at the University of South Alabama. He is a past director of Ecumenical Ministries, Inc., an organization which aids low income families in Baldwin County, and he has been active in numerous charitable and civic organizations, including the Boy Scouts of America, the American Red Cross and the Waterfront Rescue Mission. He co-leads Crown/Compass Financial Ministries small group Bible studies each year and plays music at Spanish Fort United Methodist Church and Church of the Apostles, an Anglican church in Fairhope, where he is a member.

attorneys.name: Christina D. Crow
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Montgomery, AL
attorneys.bio:
Born the youngest of three girls to Roy and Carolyn Crow in Fresno, California, Christy’s father’s Alabama roots drew them back home to Hamilton when Christy was a small child. Christy spent the majority of her formative years in Prattville, where she graduated from high school in 1990.

After graduating with a Bachelor of Science in Accounting from Auburn in 1994, Christy attended the University of Alabama School of Law and graduated in 1997 and began practicing law with the firm now known as Jinks Crow.

With over 25 years of experience in civil litigation, Christy has represented individuals and families throughout Alabama and Georgia in claims involving personal injuries, wrongful death, product liability, class actions, agricultural law, warranty violations, and a variety of other claims. She has served in leadership in MDLs. Christy has also defended local Bullock County companies in litigation and, as with most small-town lawyers, she has ended up doing a little bit of everything in her law practice.

Christy served as the President of the Alabama State Bar in 2019-2020. Her dedication to the profession was shown before that when she served as the second female President of YLS of the Bar in 2005-2006, the Women’s Section treasurer from 2009 to 2019, and a Bar Commissioner from the Third Judicial Circuit from 2007 to 2016. She has also worked on and chaired a variety of Bar task forces and committees, served on the Executive Committees of two presidents and served as Vice President of the Bar in 2012-2013. Christy also served on a Bar Disciplinary Panel from 2009 to 2011, on the Disciplinary Commission from 2011 to 2015, as Chair of the Disciplinary Commission from 2015-2016 and as chair of the Bar’s Pro Bono Celebration Task Force in 2016.

Christy is currently serving as the Secretary of Alabama Association for Justice and as the Vice President of the Southeastern Chapters of the American Board of Trial Advocates (SEABOTA).

Christy is a member of the American Board of Trial Advocates, the American Bar Association, the Alabama Association for Justice and AIEG. Christy is a Fellow of the Alabama Law Foundation, where she previously served on the Board, and a Fellow of the American Bar Foundation. She is a graduate of Class 3 of the Alabama State Bar Leadership Forum and the 2009 Class of Leadership Alabama. She currently serves on the Board of the Alabama Civil Justice Foundation, Girl Scouts of Southern Alabama and the Board of Trustees for the Alabama/West Florida United Methodist Conference.

Christy is the recipient of a variety of awards from the profession and her community, including the Bill Scruggs Service to the Bar Award from the Alabama State Bar, the Judges Award of Merit from the Alabama Judges Association, Leading Ladies award from the Girl Scouts of Southern Alabama, and the Spirit Award from the Bullock County Tourism Council.

Christy and her husband, Van Wadsworth, continue to live in Union Springs and have three children and a son-in-law.

attorneys.bio:
Defense Lawyer - Russell Crumbley at Crumbley-Blackwell & Associates, P.C. grew up in Huntsville, Alabama. Over the years Mr. Crumbley has developed a broad range of experience, knowledge, and understanding in the paramedical, scientific, and legal fields. He spent thirteen (13) years working in the medical field as a Radiologic Technologist. Most of Mr. Crumbley's efforts during this time period were spent in the surgical and emergency suites of local hospitals. During this period, he developed a solid understanding of the limits of the human body as well as various procedures within the medical field. He also completed undergraduate studies and obtained his law degree during this time period.

Upon obtaining a degree in Chemistry / Biochemistry from the University of Alabama in Huntsville, Mr. Crumbley then consulted with different attorneys in and about North Alabama where he was able to apply his understanding of medical and scientific principles.

After obtaining his law degree, he began representing clients with needs in the areas of law in which he practices today. Mr. Crumbley is admitted to the Alabama Bar and U.S. District Court, Northern District of Alabama. Mr. Crumbley is a member of the Huntsville-Madison County Bar Association, the Alabama State Bar Association, the American Bar Association, and the Alabama Criminal Defense Lawyers Association.
